name: Pain Threshold Elevation
description: Modifies pain receptor sensitivity and neural pain processing to elevate the user's pain threshold significantly without eliminating pain awareness. The user still feels pain — they know when they're injured — but the sensation is reduced to a manageable signal rather than an overwhelming experience. A broken bone registers as firm pressure rather than agony. A burn feels warm and insistent rather than excruciating. The modification preserves the protective function of pain (you know you're damaged) while removing its debilitating effects (you can still function while damaged). Crucible Genomics' version includes a 'gate override' that allows voluntary restoration of full pain sensation — useful for medical examinations where pain location matters. Street versions lack this override, leaving users permanently dulled, which leads to injuries being ignored until they become critical.
source_organism: Heterocephalus glaber (naked mole rat, reduced pain sensitivity genes)
legality: Licensed (regulated); unregulated versions monitored due to self-harm risk
procedure: Neural retroviral treatment targeting nociceptor sensitivity, 2 sessions
side_effects: Risk of ignoring serious injuries — reduced pain means reduced warning
Difficulty communicating injury severity to medical personnel
Street versions: no gate override means no way to feel what a doctor needs you to feel
Emotional blunting — some users report reduced emotional intensity alongside physical pain reduction
Rare: complete pain elimination in damaged nerve paths, creating truly insensate zones
social_perception: Common and practical in physical occupations. Fighters, laborers, and chronic pain sufferers value it highly. Medical professionals worry about users who can't feel when something is seriously wrong. The modification is considered responsible in its regulated form and dangerous in its street form.
story_hooks: A Pain Gate user is found dead from injuries they should have noticed hours earlier — their modification was working perfectly, which is exactly why they didn't seek help until it was too late

A street Pain Gate installation eliminates pain so completely that the user begins engaging in increasingly dangerous behavior — not for thrill-seeking, but because their brain has lost the feedback loop that teaches caution
